newsitem.title: USA: Southern Carolina to buy United Carolina for $985 million.
newsitem.headline: Southern Carolina to buy United Carolina for $985 million.

text.p: Southern National Corp. said Monday it will acquire United Carolina Bancshares Corp. in a stock transaction valued at $985 million.
Following the news United Carolina's stock jumped $9.50 at $37 on the Nasdaq market, while Southern National was off $1.215 at $34.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The deal calls for United Carolina stockholders to receive 1.135 shares of Southern National for each share they own, the banks said in a joint statement.
Based on Southern National's closing price Friday of $35.25, each United Carolina share would be worth $40.01 in the merger, the companies said.

The merger between the North Carolina-based banks will form a financial institution with more than $25 billion in assets. Southern National has its headquarters in Winston-Salem, while United Carolina's home base is Whiteville.
The banks said their boards of directors have unanimously approved the transaction, which is still subject to approval by their stockholders.

United Carolina said its banking subsidiaries -- United Carolina Bank and United Carolina Bank of South Carolina -- will merge into Branch Banking and Trust Company and Branch Banking and Trust Company of South Carolina, respectively, the principal banking subsidiaries of Southern National.
Southern National has 425 bank branches in the Carolinas and Virginia, while United Carolina has 153 branches in North and South Carolina.
